Provenance of this fixture
==========================

Authored inside this repository for the R15 round-trip test. It contains no
private vault material, no personal notes and no credentials: every sentence is
written for the test, and the three note/canvas files are small on purpose.

Contents
--------

  notes/index.md          hub note: wiki-links, aliases, a heading anchor, a block
                          reference, an embed, a markdown link to the canvas, an
                          external link, a callout and a task list
  notes/atomic.md         target note: the heading and the block id that index.md
                          points at (including the reverse reference)
  attachments/diagram.png a 1x1 PNG, generated for this fixture; its bytes are not
                          valid UTF-8, so a byte-level round-trip is meaningful
  vault.canvas            JSON Canvas 1.0 document (nodes and edges) with no ingest
                          route in vNext: it is custody-only material
  PROVENANCE.txt          this file

What the test proves
--------------------

`crates/archeaxis-archive/tests/obsidian_vault_roundtrip.rs` imports every file
above into a real vNext workspace, exports an archive, restores it into a fresh
workspace, and then asserts:

  * every file is byte-identical afterwards (read back through the raw object
    store by digest, not from this directory);
  * the links resolve inside the fixture itself - a wiki-link, an aliased
    wiki-link, a heading anchor, a block reference, an embed and a relative
    markdown link all point at files, headings and blocks that exist, while an
    http link is treated as external and is not required to resolve;
  * what vNext does *not* model yet is stated as an assertion rather than a
    silence: no anchor rows are written for these sources, no table stores a
    link or embed relationship, and `.canvas` has no ingest route, so it is
    preserved as bytes only.

The last group is the honest half: a passing round-trip here is a statement about
bytes, names and text, not a claim that the link graph or the canvas semantics
have been absorbed.
